taxonomy.accepted_name: Gonolobus suberosus var. granulatus (Scheele) Krings & Q.Y.Xiang
synonyms: Matelea gonocarpos (Walter) Shinners (legacy name applied to differing concepts)
taxonomy.note: Current Kew/FNA/ITIS place the Texas anglepod concept in Gonolobus suberosus var. granulatus. Texas sources often synonymize Matelea gonocarpos with this variety, but NatureServe notes the legacy name has been applied to differing concepts.

evidence: Travis — UT PRC herbarium explicitly lists Gonolobus suberosus var. granulatus.
Williamson — UT PRC county treatment explicitly treats G. suberosus var. granulatus and gives Matelea gonocarpos as a synonym.
Kerr — older TPWD Kerr WMA flora lists Matelea gonocarpos, but the legacy name has been applied to differing concepts; Kerr is not counted until concept reconciliation.
Hays — project source pool flags Hays Local under Matelea gonocarpos, but the underlying record has not yet been reconciled to var. granulatus and is not counted.
target_zone_range.blocking_issue: Two target counties are firm; legacy Matelea gonocarpos records in Kerr/Hays require taxonomic-concept reconciliation before a third county can be counted.
target_zone_range.guardrail: No county inferred from statewide or ecoregion range. Legacy names are counted only where taxonomic concept is reconciled.

morphology.look_here_first: Look for the big green anglepod: a vigorous climber with large cordate leaves, clusters of relatively large uniformly olive-green star flowers, and a smooth long follicle with sharp longitudinal angles.
diagnostic_traits: vigorous perennial twiner climbing several meters
flowers roughly 16–25 mm across in Williamson treatment
uniform olive-green glabrous corolla lobes in var. granulatus
large smooth angular follicle rather than a muricate pod

confusers.separator: Var. granulatus has uniformly olive-green glabrous lobes and yellow dorsal anther appendages; var. suberosus usually has maroon/brown lobe bases with green/yellow tips and dark purple/maroon appendages.
Pearl milkvine has smaller strongly reticulate flowers, a silvery center, and a muricate follicle; anglepod has larger uniform-green flowers and smooth sharply angled fruit.

installation_guardrail: Do not install until range ambiguity is resolved or Calvin explicitly approves an exception.
